title: SKYWARN Net: Spotter Brennan-14 Confirms Tornado at Pine Hollow

fields.centerName: BCEMA SKYWARN Net / Brennan County EOC

lines.text: Exercise, exercise, exercise. Brennan EOC, Brennan SKYWARN net control, with priority traffic.
Net control, Brennan EOC. Go ahead with your priority traffic.

Brennan EOC, this is Lena Brooks at net control. Spotter Brennan-14 is a trained spotter. He reports a rain-wrapped tornado lit up by power flashes. It's crossing the Clarks River near Pine Hollow, about four miles southwest of Corwin, and moving northeast. He can see debris in the lightning. I've relayed it to Paducah on NWSChat and by phone.
Copy, net control. Confirmed tornado near Pine Hollow, four miles southwest of Corwin, moving northeast. Where is Brennan-14 now?
Brennan-14 is south of the path and staying put. He's lost sight of it in the rain. That's all he can give us. Net control standing by.

Brennan EOC, net control again. Paducah just put out a severe weather statement on tornado warning zero zero seven one. Tornado is now OBSERVED, confirmed near Pine Hollow, four southwest of Corwin, northeast at sixty miles an hour. Damage threat is still considerable, and the warning runs until eleven fifteen. Paducah also says on NWSChat that there's a debris signature on correlation coefficient sitting right on the couplet over Pine Hollow. Exercise traffic. Net control clear.
Copy all, net control. OBSERVED, debris signature over Pine Hollow, until eleven fifteen. Brennan EOC clear.

fields.voiceStyle: Net control: woman in her fifties, experienced ham operator, steady and clipped, urgent but controlled, speaking quickly over the repeater. EOC voice: calm, flat, reads back.

instructorNote: Play the audio. At 22:47, show the SVSPAH printout and the simulated KPAH 0446Z CC figure (debris signature over Pine Hollow) on the main screen. Check four things: the 911 Supervisor confirms the North zone tone is repeating and decides under BWN 3 whether to sound the East zone, which is downstream, before it is warned. The Warning Officer logs the OBSERVED tag and sends an updated BrennanAlert, knowing N-07 at Pine Hollow is silent. The Field IC keeps crews out of the path and pre-plans for Pine Hollow. Channel 6 airs the OBSERVED tag with credit to the spotter and NWS and gives Corwin arrival times as estimates (about 4 minutes away at 60 mph).
